AboutPage.title: About Me - Max Zhang
AboutPage.role: AI Full-Stack Engineer / Multi-Agent System Conductor
AboutPage.description:
I've written a lot of code. But what keeps me up at night isn't the code.

It's an illusion. The moment I stare at the terminal and it runs through, I think the job is done.

My first job was in 2016. No mentor. No Jira tickets broken down for me. No one telling me which step goes to which role. The company threw me a module: the resource system. Frontend file upload, server-side receipt, AWS S3 storage, PostgreSQL metadata, frontend rendering — the entire chain. I was the one drawing the flowchart, the one writing the upload component, the server routes, the S3 client, the SQL migration.

Back then I didn't know this was called ReAct — think one step, do one step, check the result, think the next step. I didn't know this would later be called Planner + Executor decoupling in Agent architecture. I only knew one thing: the goal was set, and I had to walk it from end to end. The brain was mine. The hands were mine.

A decade has passed. The things I face have changed — chaining pipelines became MCP and A2A, thinking-then-doing became ReAct, manual documentation lookup became RAG. What I'm driving isn't my own two hands anymore — it's a legion of expert-level Agents, forged into a self-sufficient army. But the mindset hasn't changed.

What does this thing look like.

It's not a chat box. Chat boxes are dead. I ask, it answers, conversation over. The light goes out, and the mind goes with it. What I want is a light that never goes out. Something alive. It perceives, it decides, it acts. I draw a line — it runs within it.

Decades of AI accumulation have finally reached the Agent stage. The earliest expert systems were just machines reciting from a rulebook. Give it rules, it follows them — never taking one step more. Then came reinforcement learning, pushing the limits within narrow domains, beating humans at Go, crushing pros at Dota. But it couldn't leave that field. Step off the board and it couldn't even walk.

Until now. LLMs can understand vague intent. They can decompose a messy requirement into twelve steps. They can invoke external tools. They can pause mid-execution to think. They can self-correct. They can shape the output into the format I need. It's not some black magic — it just chained together understanding, planning, execution, and feedback, linked the four rings, and set them spinning.

Many fear it replacing them.

Hell no, not even close.

I've tried dumping an ambiguous requirement straight at it. It does produce output. But would I dare use it directly? I don't know what it skipped, misunderstood, or ignored. Twelve steps run doesn't mean every step is right. It needs someone standing above, setting direction, drawing boundaries.

But it lets me — one person — achieve the throughput of a team. An orchestrator Agent handles decomposition and decision-making. A swarm of specialist Agents each owns their domain, advancing in parallel. Retrieval retrieving, execution executing, verification verifying. They don't wait on each other. They don't interrupt each other. No coffee, no emotions. They just do what they're best at, then stitch the results back into a complete answer.

This is the new paradigm of human-machine collaboration as I see it. Not automation — that's a word from twenty years ago. Not replacement — that's a fear-driven narrative. It's leverage. It's amplification. I call the shots. They fight my battles.

When I write this, what's in my mind isn't architecture diagrams or tech selection tables. It's that version of me sitting at the desk in 2016, facing a chain I'd never walked before, from frontend to database, carrying it alone from beginning to end. Back then he didn't know what he was writing was called "engineering thinking." He was just using one brain and two hands to hold up an entire module from end to end.

Now I know. Now those hands can be an army of Agents.

What I'm writing isn't code. Code goes obsolete, frameworks iterate, APIs get deprecated. I'm writing the productivity infrastructure of the next decade. It's the boundary of output that one person plus an Agent legion can pry open. It's the thrust that pushes every industry forward, centimeter by centimeter, through the gears of a thousand trades.

Not AI that replaces people. AI that amplifies people.

Not a system that chats. A system that works.

It's not the future. It's the present.

experience.role: Frontend Lead / AI Full-Stack Engineer / MAS Conductor
experience.company: Chengdu Ruisheng Tianhe Media Technology Co., Ltd.
points: Designed and built a multi-agent collaboration system around ReAct planning-execution architecture, enabling task decomposition, tool orchestration, and context management with dynamic MCP tool integration.
Built A2A distributed agent networks, connecting planning and execution agents for task dispatch and result aggregation.
Developed Docker sandbox isolation environments for secure code execution — Shell commands, Python scripts, and Playwright browser automation run in isolated containers.

Led the company's digital advertising platform, connecting asset production, approvals, campaign delivery, and data feedback into an online workflow, supporting 100,000 videos and 30,000+ images per month with 80%+ efficiency gains.

Pioneered AI-native engineering workflows — integrated Codex, Claude, and in-house MCP to automate requirement drafting, task breakdown, execution validation, and bug fixing, reducing per-video generation cost from RMB 2.5–3 to RMB 0.5–1.
Led engineering governance for multiple legacy internal systems, including build upgrades, component refactoring, monorepo restructuring, and team-wide standards.

Worked across domestic and international teams on multilingual, multi-line-of-business delivery, spanning requirement analysis, implementation, and gradual evolution toward modular and microservice-based systems.
Maintained and iterated on more than 20 legacy frontend and backend projects, driving incremental refactors across React Native, Vue, React, Nest.js, PHP, and MongoDB.
Led a four-person team to rewrite a high-traffic user-facing product area and improved foundational capabilities such as RBAC, JWT auth, environment management, exception handling, and rate limiting.
Participated in microservice and distributed-systems work covering health checks, circuit breaking, Consul, Docker, SMS, caching, email, and scheduled task modules.
Independently delivered the BD Policy Manager web app and WeChat H5 product from 0 to 1, translating client needs into product and engineering solutions.

Built a distributed crawling system with Python, Scrapy, Redis, and Django to ingest millions of insurance clauses, including login simulation, CAPTCHA handling, cookie pools, and incremental crawling.

Handled product demos and client presentations for hundreds of participants, and established a training pipeline that turned interns with no experience into independent contributors within six months.

experience.company: Chengdu Shulian Yixin Technology Co., Ltd.
points: Worked on hospital device data cleansing and forwarding systems, owning the end-to-end delivery of Yixin Cloud Service resources from frontend to backend.
Enabled SMB support in PHP7 by compiling a C module, which made Windows log forwarding from hospital intranets to Linux systems possible.
Contributed to the SaaS platform and WeChat H5 apps, and helped deliver Yixin Cloud Service 2.0 on schedule for key product and fundraising milestones.
